svg.title: rEach and Teach: trust boundaries
svg.desc: The student's computer, the private course server, the AI provider and GitHub are separate zones. Seven numbered crossings show what moves between them and how each is protected.
svg.text: Four zones, seven crossings. Everything between the computer and the course server is signed, sealed or both.
The assistant the student already uses.
rEach's hooks sit on every prompt,
Install key: made here, never leaves
Sign-in check value, never the password
The plugin and its pinned kits
Owned files: the agent may write
course server · private to the instructors
each reveal of a name is logged
sees the chat, as with any assistant
releases, updates, runtime and SDK kits
Each request carries a signature from the install's
own RSA-4096 key and a digest of the computer's
AES-256-GCM, with the key wrapped for this one
install. Verified before a single byte is unpacked.
Owned files and a manifest, sealed to the course
server's key, and only after the student says yes.
Proof of what arrived and when. rEach verifies each
receipt before it tells the student anything.
Signed-in assignment work only, about every ten
minutes, under a pseudonym with the names rEach
Goes to the student's AI provider, as any chat does,
rEach follows the stable branch. The runtime and SDK
kits are verified against manifests pinned in rEach.
